cards.text: Isaiah, the prophet, has a message, and it opens with one word: "Woe." It's for people who go down to Egypt for help. Friend, when a prophet opens with "Woe," you do NOT want to be the one he's talking about.

cards.question: These people going down to Egypt rely on horses, and they trust in their abundance of ___.
True or false: While they trust in all those horsemen from Egypt, they're also seeking the LORD.

cards.text: I bet those folks feel REAL smart counting all those chariots. But Isaiah says the LORD is wise too, and He brings disaster.

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD is wise and brings disaster. What does Isaiah say about the LORD's words?

answers.text: He does not call them back

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD will rise up against the house of the wicked. Who else does He rise up against?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says it plain, and I LOVE how plain he says it: "But the Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit."

cards.question: When the LORD stretches out His hand, what happens to Egypt the helper and the people it's helping?

cards.text: Both of them, DOWN, together. Then the prophet says the LORD gave him a picture: a young lion over its prey, and a whole band of shepherds called out, shouting at it.

cards.question: True or false: All that shouting from the band of shepherds terrifies the lion.
A dozen shepherds yelling, and that lion doesn't budge. So, like that lion, what does the LORD of Hosts come down to do on Mount Zion?

cards.text: Then the picture changes. The lion's gone, and now there are birds hovering overhead.

cards.question: Like birds hovering overhead, the LORD of Hosts will ___ Jerusalem.

cards.text: Hovering. That's me at the oven window with a fresh batch inside, and NOBODY is touching that tray. "He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it."
Now Isaiah speaks straight to the children of Israel, and he names what they've done: they've rebelled against the LORD.

cards.question: Isaiah tells the children of Israel they've rebelled against the LORD. What does he call them to do?

cards.text: And he doesn't tiptoe, either. Not a little rebellion, friend: BLATANTLY. But Isaiah says a day is coming when every one of them will let something go.

cards.question: On that day, every one of the children of Israel will reject the ___ of silver and gold their own hands made.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about Assyria, a mighty empire. Assyria will fall.

cards.question: The LORD says Assyria will fall. How?

answers.text: Not by a sword of man

cards.question: True or false: When that sword comes, Assyria stands its ground and fights it out.

cards.text: They run, and it gets worse from there. Their young men will be put to forced labor, and their rock will pass away for fear.

cards.question: Assyria's princes panic. What sets them off?

answers.text: The sight of the battle standard
The roar of a young lion

cards.text: The LORD signs off this way: His fire is in Zion, His furnace is in Jerusalem. Friend, I know ovens, and I would NOT want to be on the wrong side of THAT one.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "The shepherds of Bethlehem" and "The fishermen of Galilee" are harmless groups with no tie to wickedness. That leaves "The allies of evildoers" as the only answer that fits "the house of the wicked," so the right answer stands out and the card gives away its own answer. The wrong answers should be believable groups the LORD might rise up against, or allies the passage could plausibly name, such as "the kings of the nations" or "the priests of Baal."

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer "Both of them fall" doesn't match the text. Isaiah 31:3 says the helper will stumble, the one he helps will fall, and both will perish together. It doesn't say both fall. The answer should use the text's word, as in "Both of them perish." Card 9's line "Both of them, DOWN, together" works either way.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "A dozen shepherds yelling" adds a number the text doesn't give. Isaiah 31:4 says only "a band of shepherds." The line is in the question and reads as a fact, not as one of Papa Dorin's jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: "When that sword comes" points back to the sword in card 6's answer, which is no longer on screen. The question should say what the sword is, for example: "The LORD says a sword not made by mortals will devour Assyria. True or false: Assyria stands its ground and fights it out."

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "The LORD signs off this way: His fire is in Zion, His furnace is in Jerusalem" has the LORD saying the fire and furnace line. In Isaiah 31:9, the quote ends with "declares the LORD." The line that follows, "whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem," describes the LORD. It isn't something He says. The card could say the LORD declares it, the LORD whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
